title: 2000 AMC 12 Problem 17
statement: A circle centered at \(O\) has radius \(1\) and contains the point \(A.\) Segment \(AB\) is tangent to the circle at \(A\) and \(\angle AOB = \theta.\) If point \(C\) lies on \(\overline{OA}\) and \(BC\) bisects \(\angle ABO,\) then what is \(OC?\)

solutions.text:
Because \(OA = 1\) and \(AB\) is tangent at \(A,\) angle \(OAB\) is right, so \[ BA = \tan\theta, \qquad OB = \sec\theta. \]

Since \(BC\) bisects \(\angle ABO,\) the angle bisector theorem gives \(\dfrac{OC}{CA} = \dfrac{OB}{BA}.\) Using \(OC + CA = OA = 1,\) \[ \begin{aligned} OC &= \frac{OB}{OB + BA} \\ &= \frac{\sec\theta}{\sec\theta + \tan\theta}. \end{aligned} \]

Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\cos\theta\) gives \(OC = \dfrac{1}{1 + \sin\theta}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Since \(OA = 1\) and \(\angle OAB = 90^\circ,\) we have \(BA = \tan\theta\) and \(OB = \sec\theta\)
The bisector gives \(\dfrac{OC}{CA} = \dfrac{OB}{BA},\) and \(OC + CA = OA = 1\)
